jobs.occupation: Senior Scientist, Downstream, Late-Stage Process Development
jobs.description:
Join a fast-paced process development team where scientific expertise, collaboration and practical problem-solving help advance projects. As Senior Scientist, you will lead downstream development activities for mammalian cell culture processes, supporting their progression through late-stage development.

You will work closely with clients, laboratory technicians and colleagues across upstream, downstream and analytical disciplines. The role combines scientific leadership, study design, data interpretation and technical writing. Most hands-on laboratory work will be performed by technicians; you will work closely with them to develop protocols, design experiments and guide execution, ensuring studies are scientifically sound and generate decision-quality data.

**A role with scientific ownership and real project impact

**As a Senior Scientist, you will have the opportunity to take ownership of downstream development activities and contribute directly to the progression of projects. You will combine your scientific expertise with practical problem-solving and collaborate with both internal colleagues and clients.

The role gives you exposure to different projects, technologies and challenges rather than focusing on one narrow area. You will be involved in shaping studies, interpreting data and turning scientific findings into clear recommendations that support project decisions.

Your work will also give you the opportunity to collaborate closely with laboratory technicians and scientists, allowing you to stay connected to the practical side of process development while taking a leading role in the scientific direction.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Lead and coordinate downstream development activities for assigned projects, working with clients and cross-functional teams to align on project needs and deliver outcomes.

• Plan and evaluate downstream processes, including chromatography using ÄKTA systems and filtration operations such as depth filtration, virus filtration and ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF).

• Design studies and author practical protocols in close collaboration with laboratory technicians; provide scientific guidance during experimental execution.

• Interpret study results, apply appropriate statistical approaches—including design of experiments (DoE) where relevant—and communicate findings through clear presentations and reports.

• Contribute to process characterization, including failure mode and risk assessments such as FMEA, and author process characterization (PC) work reports.

• Support investigations and deviation handling by assessing technical causes, interpreting relevant data, and documenting conclusions and follow-up actions.

• Provide scientific and technical input to business activities and support the generation of information for regulatory submissions.

**Required Qualifications And Experience

**

• Education: Master’s or PhD in Biochemistry, Biochemical or Chemical Engineering, Process Technology, or a related discipline.

• Industrial experience: 5+ years with a Master’s degree, or 2+ years with a PhD.

• Downstream development: Demonstrated experience with mammalian cell culture processes.

• Unit operations: Chromatography and filtration; ideally ÄKTA systems and TFF systems.

• Study execution and data: Ability to plan, analyze and report complex development studies, including statistical analysis.

• Project work: Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities with scientific rigour and attention to detail.

• Communication: Strong interpersonal skills and ability to explain technical findings clearly to clients and colleagues.

• Language: Fluent written and spoken English.

**Preferred Qualifications And Experience

**

• Process Characterization and FMEA

• Viral clearance studies or activities.

• Commercial manufacturing requirements and biologics regulatory frameworks, including relevant ICH guidelines and BLA submission requirements.

• Knowledge of Design of Experiments (DoE), including experimental design, data analysis, and evaluation using SAS JMP

• Liquid-handling automation, such as Tecan systems.

**What Will Help You Succeed

**You take ownership, bring a practical can-do attitude and are comfortable working at pace. You collaborate closely with technicians and colleagues, communicate openly, and use data and sound scientific judgement to find a way forward as project needs and priorities evolve.

**What You Can Expect From Us

**We want you to have the opportunity to use your scientific expertise while continuing to develop professionally. In this role, you can expect:

• Scientific ownership: Take responsibility for development activities and influence how studies are designed and executed.

• Variety: Work across different projects, technologies and scientific challenges rather than doing the same thing every day.

• Cross-functional collaboration: Work closely with scientists, technicians, upstream and analytical colleagues as well as clients.

• Client exposure: Develop your ability to communicate scientific findings and recommendations directly with clients and contribute to project discussions.

• Professional development: Continue developing your expertise in downstream processing, process characterization, data analysis and late-stage development.

• Impact: See how your scientific work contributes to advancing biopharmaceutical processes towards later-stage development and manufacturing.

**A team where science and collaboration go hand in hand

**You will become part of a team where scientific knowledge, practical experience and collaboration are important to how we work. We value people who share knowledge, ask questions and are willing to challenge and support each other.

You will work closely with experienced colleagues across different disciplines, giving you the opportunity to learn from others while also bringing your own expertise to the team.

We believe that good science is strengthened by open communication, different perspectives and a willingness to find solutions together.

**Ready to make your next move?

**If you are looking for a role where you can combine scientific expertise, project ownership, client interaction and practical problem-solving, we would like to hear from you.

Apply through the AGC Biologics career site by **31 October 2026.

**Please note that we only accept applications through our recruitment system and cannot accept CVs by email.

**The Recruitment Process Will Include

**

• An initial screening interview with People & Culture

• An interview with the Hiring Manager

• A final interview, including a cognitive assessment and personality assessment

• A meet and greet with team members and a laboratory tour

• Reference checks

Applications will be reviewed on a continuous basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. We may close the position before the application deadline once the right candidate has been identified.

_Location: We can only consider candidates currently based in Denmark or the Greater Malmö area, as relocation support is not available for this position.

_At AGC Biologics, we are committed to a fair and unbiased recruitment process. We assess candidates based on their skills, experience, qualifications, and potential to succeed in the role.

To support an objective recruitment process, please do not include a photo in your application or CV.

**Who We Are

**AGC Biologics is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization with a strong presence in Denmark. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market.

About MITS Industries

MITS Industries is establishing an R&D and design site in Copenhagen focused on advanced RF systems, signal intelligence, aerospace technologies, and mission-critical product development.

The site will build core engineering capabilities in RF and microwave hardware, antenna systems, RF testing and characterization, rugged mechanical integration, and the industrialization of complex radio-electronic systems.

The Copenhagen team will work closely with strategic partners and engineering teams across Europe, playing a leading role in the development, validation, and industrialization of advanced technologies for defense, aerospace, and other demanding applications.

One of the initial focus areas will be the development of an advanced aerospace signal intelligence product platform. The work will cover RF and system architecture, antenna system design, signal acquisition, embedded control, laboratory validation, mechanical integration, integration with the satellite platform, and preparation for production and field deployment.

The ambition is to build a strong technical design site capable of taking complex RF products, modules, and platforms from architecture and detailed design through prototyping, testing, validation, industrialization, and deployment.

About the role

MITS Industries is looking for a Senior RF / Microwave Hardware Engineer to join the core Copenhagen R&D team and help build the site’s RF and microwave design capability.

You will design and develop RF and microwave hardware and subsystems, including receiver front ends, amplification, filtering, mixers and local-oscillator circuitry, RF signal routing, and PCB- and module-level implementation. The work covers RF performance analysis and design trade-offs, circuit architecture, schematic design, component selection, circuit and electromagnetic simulation, RF PCB implementation and layout, prototyping, debugging, and performance validation.

You will work closely with system architects, antenna systems engineers, SDR and signal processing engineers, RF test and characterization engineers, mechanical design engineers, and partner engineering teams. The role requires deep RF and microwave design expertise, technical ownership, and hands-on implementation experience, taking designs from concept through prototyping and validation to documented, manufacturable RF modules and subsystems.

Key responsibilities

• Translate system requirements into RF hardware architecture, specifications, performance budgets, and design trade-offs.

• Design RF and microwave circuits, modules, and signal-acquisition paths, including amplification, filtering, switching, mixing, frequency synthesis, gain control, and supporting bias, power, and control circuitry.

• Perform RF performance analysis covering sensitivity, selectivity, gain, noise figure, dynamic range, linearity, stability, spurious responses, and interference resilience.

• Create RF schematics, select components, and own RF PCB implementation, including laminate and material selection, stack-up definition, and layout, with controlled-impedance routing, transmission lines, grounding, shielding, isolation, and high-frequency interconnects.

• Perform circuit and electromagnetic simulations, optimize designs, and correlate simulated performance with laboratory measurements.

• Lead prototypes bring-up, tuning, debugging, and design verification in collaboration with RF test and characterization engineers.

• Integrate RF hardware with antenna systems, data-conversion interfaces, mechanical assemblies, and platform interfaces.

• Contribute to design verification, EMC/EMI assessment, environmental qualification, reliability evaluation, and system-level validation.

• Prepare hardware specifications, design documentation, BOMs, analysis reports, design-review materials, test inputs, and production-release documentation.

• Own technical decisions related to component and supplier selection, manufacturability, testability, lifecycle risks, and design-risk mitigation.

• Collaborate with system, antenna, signal-processing, test, mechanical, manufacturing, and partner engineering teams.

Required qualifications and experience

• Master’s degree in electrical or electronic engineering, RF/microwave engineering, applied physics, or a related field. A PhD is an advantage.

• 7+ years of professional experience in RF and microwave hardware design.

• Strong hands-on experience developing RF circuits, multilayer PCBs, modules, and subsystems from schematic design and simulation through layout, bring-up, tuning, and validation.

• Experience with receiver architectures and RF signal paths, including low-noise and gain stages, filters, switches, mixers, oscillators, PLL-based frequency synthesis, and supporting bias, power, and control circuitry.

• Strong understanding of RF system budgeting, chain analysis, and frequency planning, including gain, noise figure, sensitivity, selectivity, dynamic range, P1dB, IP3, phase noise, stability, spurious responses, isolation, and impedance matching.

• Practical experience with RF PCB implementation, including laminate and material selection, stack-up definition, controlled-impedance routing, transmission lines, grounding, shielding, isolation, and high-frequency interconnects.

• Hands-on experience with schematic capture and RF PCB layout using an industry standard ECAD tool such as Altium Designer, Cadence Allegro/OrCAD, or equivalent.

• Proficiency with one or more RF circuit and electromagnetic simulation tools, such as Keysight ADS, Cadence AWR Microwave Office, Ansys HFSS, or CST Studio Suite.

• Hands-on experience with RF measurement equipment, including vector network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and oscilloscopes.

• Demonstrated ability to bring up, tune, troubleshoot, and validate RF hardware and correlate measured results with simulations.

• Experience taking RF hardware through prototype manufacturing, assembly, design verification, environmental requirements and qualification, and production release.

Nice to have

• Experience with signal-intelligence, direction-finding, spectrum-monitoring, or radio-surveillance systems.

• Experience with SDR-based radio architecture.

• Experience designing wideband, high-dynamic-range, low-noise receiver systems.

• Experience with coherent or multichannel RF systems, including channel matching, phase stability, and synchronization.

• Experience developing aerospace, mission-critical, or ruggedized electronic systems.

• Experience developing RF and microwave hardware operating at frequencies up to and beyond 18GHz.

Success in the first 6 months

• Take technical ownership of one or more RF modules or subsystem areas.

• Establish the initial architecture, design approach, and development plan for the assigned RF scope.

• Deliver reviewed schematics, simulations, layout inputs, and supporting design documentation.

• Bring up and validate initial hardware prototypes, with clear correlation between expected and measured performance.

• Identify key RF, implementation, and integration risks and define practical mitigation actions.

• Establish effective technical interfaces with system, antenna, signal-processing, test, mechanical, manufacturing, and partner engineering teams.

jobs.occupation: Test Method Specialist, Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory
jobs.description:
_**Imagine if robust test methods and reliable test equipment helped ensure the quality of both new and existing Coloplast products. That is where you come in.

**_As our new Test Method Specialist, you will become the technical focal point for selected test methods and related equipment in Coloplast Mørdrup, primarily supporting the QA Lifecycle Laboratory and Pilot SVS. This is a practical, hands-on specialist role in which you will work directly with laboratory equipment, including troubleshooting, service and calibration follow-up, qualification, and software and computer upgrades. You will support the full test method and equipment lifecycle, from implementation and qualification to maintenance, transfer and continuous improvement.

If you are motivated by hands-on technical problem-solving, equipment responsibility, quality assurance and data evaluation, this role offers meaningful responsibility and broad organisational impact. You will also work closely with many internal and external stakeholders, making clear communication, coordination and strong stakeholder management an important part of your success.

_“In this role, your technical judgement and ability to create robust solutions will help ensure reliable test results and compliant laboratory processes throughout the product lifecycle,” says Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory.

_**Join a skilled and collaborative laboratory team

**At our Coloplast Mørdrup site, you will join the Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory. The team consists of laboratory technicians and test method specialists who work closely together to support ongoing production, process development, quality investigations and test method activities.

You will be part of an engaged team with a strong mix of practical laboratory experience and specialist knowledge. In our daily work, we collaborate closely with colleagues across Quality Assurance, Research and Development, Operations, Global Test Method teams and international manufacturing sites. We value curiosity, knowledge sharing, flexibility and a continuous improvement mindset.

**Own and develop test methods and equipment

**As Test Method Specialist, you will act as a one-point contact and technical superuser for selected test methods and test equipment. A significant part of the role is practical equipment responsibility. You will work hands-on with equipment and coordinate activities to ensure it is qualified, calibrated, serviced, maintained and performing as intended. You will also support software and computer upgrades connected to the equipment, as well as reliable data handling and traceability.

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• Acting as technical owner and one-point contact for selected test methods and related test equipment

• Planning, coordinating and performing qualification of test equipment, including relocation, capacity expansion and replacement of critical parts

• Preparing and maintaining qualification protocols, reports, procedures, test method documentation and one-point lessons when needed

• Performing hands-on troubleshooting of test equipment and methods, evaluating test results and leading root cause investigations when failures occur

• Taking practical responsibility for test equipment, including service activities, calibration follow-up, preventive maintenance and ensuring that equipment performs as intended

• Handling changes, nonconformities and CAPAs related to test methods, calibration and test equipment

• Supporting compliant storage and traceability of raw data before product release

• Planning and participating in transfers of test methods and equipment to international manufacturing sites

• Providing technical support and sparring to colleagues in the Pilot Plant, Global Operations and international manufacturing sites

• Collaborating with Global Test Method teams and contributing technical input to the development and improvement of test methods

• Training specialists, laboratory technicians, operators and other users in test methods, test principles and use of equipment

• Coordinating software and computer upgrades for test equipment, assessing their impact on qualification and documentation, and managing suppliers, service visits and relevant service agreements

• Participating in internal and external audits related to test methods, equipment and documentation

• Contributing to continuous improvement of laboratory processes, systems and ways of working

**Bring strong technical judgement and a quality mindset

**To succeed in this position, you combine technical depth with a structured, practical and hands-on approach. You enjoy working directly with equipment, take ownership and work systematically when resolving technical issues. You are comfortable making decisions based on data, risk and regulatory requirements.

The role involves close collaboration with many internal and external stakeholders, therefor you communicate clearly, coordinate effectively and are able to build strong working relationships across functions, sites and suppliers.

We imagine that you bring:

• A master’s degree within science, engineering, mechanics, physics, chemistry, pharmacy or a comparable technical field, or have at least five years of relevant experience with test methods

• Solid hands-on experience with test methods, measurement principles and qualification of laboratory or production test equipment

• Strong problem-solving skills and experience with structured root cause analysis

• Confident evaluating, analysing and presenting technical data skills, including the use of statistical methods

• Ability to write, review and understand technical documentation, protocols and reports

• Knowledge of quality systems and regulated environments; knowledge of ISO 9001, ISO 13485 and GMP is an advantage

• An understanding of validation, calibration, design control, specifications and process risk management

• Abitlity to plan and prioritise your work effectively and follow activities through to completion

• Strong stakeholder management skills and collaborate effectively across disciplines, functions, geographical locations and external suppliers

• Communicating skills professionally in English, both written and spoken; Danish is an advantage

• A comfortable competence using digital tools for documentation, data analysis and traceability; experience with Microsoft Office, Veeva, JMP or similar systems is an advantage

**A specialist role with broad impact

**This is a permanent specialist position in the QA Lifecycle Laboratory. The role has no direct reports and includes collaboration with international colleagues and manufacturing sites. Some travel may be expected in connection with transfers, supplier activities and site support.

You will join a working environment where quality, safety, technical excellence, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement are central to our daily work. You will have the opportunity to build a broad network and influence how test methods and equipment are managed across the product lifecycle.

**Interested?

**If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory, at dklst@coloplast.com.

jobs.occupation: Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**Overview

**The Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead plays a key leadership role in overseeing Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs) while supporting the broader Clinical Trial Management (CTM) organization. This individual ensures high-quality clinical trial execution by providing strategic guidance, mentorship, and operational oversight. The Line Manager is responsible for team development, resource allocation, process optimization, and ensuring alignment with organizational goals and regulatory standards. The Trial Delivery Team Lead may assume Global Trial Lead (GTL) responsibilities to address fluctuating demands.

**Roles & Responsibilities

****Leadership and Line Management:

**

• Directly manage, mentor, and develop Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs), fostering professional growth.

• Conduct performance evaluations, provide feedback, and identify training and career development opportunities.

• Ensure adequate resourcing, workload distribution, and succession planning within the team.

• Facilitate cross-functional collaboration and knowledge-sharing within the clinical operations team.

• Collaborate with Global Trial Leads (GTLs) on trial activities for assigned direct reports.

• Support trial deliverables by facilitating progress, coaching, and mentoring CTMs and CTAs.

• Advise on resource needs and support overall clinical trial resource planning.

• Ensure team success through setting clear expectations, guiding performance, and leading competency development.

• Lead functional working groups; serve as process owner or Subject Matter Expert (SME) within Clinical Operations.

• Support training initiatives across Trial Operations as needed.

• Collaborate with senior leadership to define and implement best practices within the Development Operations organization.

**Process & Compliance Management

**

• Ensure team adherence to Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ICH guidelines, and regulatory requirements (FDA, EMA, etc.).

• Develop and refine Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to optimize trial efficiency and compliance.

• Support audits, inspections, and regulatory interactions by ensuring inspection readiness across clinical trials.

• Identify and drive process improvements to enhance trial execution and data quality.

• Lead cross-trial initiatives as needed, such as implementation of Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs) or new process rollouts across the program.

• Manages the execution and implementation of CTM and CTA tasks, ensuring operational success.

• Initiates and supports the development of processes within the CTM and CTA group, focusing on practical application and continuous improvement.

• Collaborates across functions to drive efficiencies and provide day-to-day guidance to the CTM and CTA groups.

**Requirements – What You Must Have

**

• Bachelor of science degree with relevant specialization; Master of science degree preferred

• Minimum requirement of 12 or more years of experience in clinical operations

• Significant experience in leading and managing complex global clinical projects/programs

• Significant experience managing/guiding internal (cross-functional) and external (CRO, regulatory authorities) teams

• Experience with operational management and budget planning

• Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role

• Global clinical program level experience required

• Experience within the field of oncology is preferred

• Minimum 2 years’ experience as Clinical Operations representative in Clinical Development Teams (CDTs) or Global Project Teams (GPTs) would be preferable

• Experience leading team members in global matrix environment, leveraging tools and technology to ensure business needs are met.

• Strategic thinking with ability to optimize organizational resources for successful program execution

• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken

**Moreover, You Meet The Following Personal Requirements

**

• Dedicated team player who enjoys leading teams and inspire trust among colleagues

• Quality mindset and able to prioritize your work in a fast paced and changing environment

• Result- and goal-oriented and committed to contributing to the overall success of Genmab

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on role will be provided during the recruitment process

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.

Spare Parts Coordinator

Are you passionate about customer service, coordination, and delivering results in an international environment? We are looking for a structured and service-minded Spare Parts Coordinator to join our Customer Service team. In this role, you will play a key part in ensuring the efficient handling of spare parts inquiries, quotations, and sales orders, contributing to an excellent customer experience through professional support, proactive communication, and reliable order execution.

As a Spare Parts Coordinator, you will be responsible for managing the spare parts process from initial customer inquiry through to final delivery. • Design Patterns & Models: Develop and promote standardized design patterns and models to ensure consistent application design and a resilient, scalable architecture across the enterprise.

• Principle Custodianship: Act as the lead custodian of Satair’s signature architecture principles, ensuring every solution adheres to these guidelines.

• Continuous Improvement: Proactively identify where software, applications, or processes need to evolve to meet the needs of tomorrow’s aviation market.

In this pivotal position, you serve as a key bridge between our strategic vision and the technical execution of the IT organization. You will have a leading role in the architecture landscape, acting as the primary driver for the Architecture Board. Your work ensures that the integrity of our current technology is protected while we build the capabilities required for a secure, resilient, and sustainable future.

We are looking for a seasoned professional with a deep background in IT strategy and architecture governance. You should have a proven ability to lead through influence, gaining commitment from senior management for major technology shifts.

What you bring to the table:

• Architectural Excellence: A proven track record in developing resilient architecture models and reusable design patterns.

• Strategic Insight: The ability to perform cost/benefit evaluations that justify strategic technology choices to the CIO office and IT Management.

• Operational Focus: A commitment to ensuring technical solutions deliver on business promises and operational SLAs.

Beyond technical skills, we value individuals who bring a collaborative mindset, excellent communication abilities, and the confidence to interact with stakeholders at all levels.

In this team, we prioritize innovation, problem-solving, and proactive thinking. If you are passionate about securing the future of aviation and enjoy working in an environment that values your expertise, we’d love to hear from you.

In Satair, you can challenge the status quo, pioneer new ways of working, and generate real value for airlines and suppliers worldwide.

If you want to work as one team embracing a can-do attitude in a demanding environment, then we offer a great place to explore, learn, and grow.

As a senior member of the AI team, you will help shape how we build with Large Language Models and agentic systems across our products, contributing to high‑level design decisions, turning ambiguous business problems into robust system designs, and ensuring high‑quality coding standards and design.
